title: Realtime Multimodal Technical Support for Field Technicians
business: Industrial field service companies managing complex hardware repairs.
problem: Technicians often struggle with hands-free documentation access, leading to delays when they must manually search manuals while handling tools or equipment in low-visibility environments.
solution: The GPT-Realtime model enables a hands-free, voice-activated interface that processes audio input directly from the field, allowing technicians to ask questions and receive immediate, synthesized audio instructions without interrupting their physical workflow.
steps: Establish a persistent WebSocket connection to the gpt-realtime endpoint.
Configure the session to accept audio input streams from the technician's headset.
Define function calling tools that allow the model to query internal repair databases.
Stream the model's audio output back to the technician's device for immediate playback.
Implement prompt caching for frequently accessed equipment manuals to optimize context usage.
outcome: Technicians experience improved operational efficiency and reduced cognitive load by interacting with technical documentation through natural, conversational voice commands.
limitation: The model's reliance on continuous streaming connections means that intermittent network connectivity in remote industrial sites can cause latency or session drops; developers should monitor WebSocket heartbeat signals to detect and trigger automatic reconnection logic.
